soils.name: Dark prairie soils (Mollisols)
soils.appearance: Dark brown to black, darker still when wet.
soils.effect: Good chromatic contrast with green; deep shadows on dark soil are hard to separate from soil (both dark).

soils.name: Light loams and sandy soils
soils.effect: Clean split; Otsu about 0.27 on the close-up photo tested.

soils.name: Red, iron-rich soils
soils.effect: With straw on the surface the automatic split falls between soil and straw; the profile's index floor is needed.

residue.name: Corn stover (corn after corn)
residue.appearance: Coarse stalk pieces; old stalk rows offset about half a row from the new rows.
residue.effect: Brightness stripes at the crop pitch out of phase with the crop; straw near ExGR -0.14 stays out of the green mask, but ExG with Otsu can pick it up.

residue.name: Soybean stubble (corn after soybean)
residue.appearance: Thin grey stubble with faint drill lines; breaks down fast.
residue.effect: Weak residue signal; drill lines at the soybean's narrower pitch.

residue.name: Small-grain straw (double crop, cover crop)
residue.effect: Brightest background; the classic ExG false positive.

shadows.description: Corn casts shadows into the alley from about V5; by V8 at low sun they span a 76 cm alley. Shadow on soil is dark, not green: it inflates a not-soil cover mask but not a green mask, and it darkens weeds in the alley.
shadows.heightToShadowNote: Shadow length = plant height / tan(sun elevation): 30 cm plant 17 cm at 60° sun and 52 cm at 30°; 60 cm plant 35 and 104 cm.

evidence.notes: Geometry is our arithmetic; no corn shadow study found.

irrigation.geometryEffect: Every furrow or every other row; hard wheel-track middles and soft furrows; 40 in beds with twin rows in the South.

coverCrops.practice: Cover crops drilled into the alley at V4 to V6 (1 to 3 lines per alley)
coverCrops.effect: Deliberate green between the rows: every off-row green would read as weed. The operator must say so; the profile cannot tell from the image.

coverCrops.practice: Planting green into a living cover crop terminated after planting
coverCrops.effect: Dying cover in the alley; yellow-green cover mask lights it.

calendar.priorityStageWindow: V2 to V5 about 2 to 4 weeks after planting: mid May to late June

evidence.notes: Virginia: weed-free for the first 4 to 6 weeks.

calendar.priorityStageWindow: April to May; control 20 to 45 days after planting

calendar.plantingWindow: April to May (first crop); June to July (second crop after wheat)
calendar.priorityStageWindow: May to June; July to August for second crop

gaps: No measured index values for corn stover or soybean stubble; the residue descriptions are partly ours.
No corn shadow study; no study of planting green or interseeded alleys from the air.
Calendar windows are broad; the field's own planting date is what the profile uses.
